narrative.overview:
Mihwar should feel like a live automotive test bench: precise, technical, premium, and fast. Graphite test-bay surfaces, warm metal whites, calibrated rails, compact labels, and one controlled orange signal make product discovery feel operational rather than ornamental.

The system is Arabic-first and mobile-first, with complete LTR equivalence. Interfaces place search, vehicle guidance, practical product detail, and honest status information ahead of spectacle; the result is a focused parts counter rather than a cinematic car poster or a generic ecommerce skin.
keyCharacteristics: A single controlled orange signal with merchant-controlled accent ownership.
Squared controls, restrained curves, thin rails, ticks, and tabular numeric detail.
Dense enough to feel technical, spacious enough to scan quickly.
Short axis movement and one calibrated scan instead of ambient visual effects.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Use orange as a diagnostic signal, not as broad decoration; large surfaces remain graphite, paper, or white.

rules.name: The Merchant Accent Rule
rules.body: Commerce emphasis follows the configured merchant accent, while the fixed safety signal remains reserved for system feedback.

rules.name: The Arabic-First Rule
rules.body: Use the configured `--font-main` throughout; do not introduce a decorative Latin display face that weakens Arabic parity.

rules.name: The Short Display Rule
rules.body: Reserve the tightest tracking and leading for brief, balanced headlines; long explanatory content uses the body rhythm.

rules.name: The Task-First Breakpoint Rule
rules.body: On small screens, search and the next usable action precede visual inspection; wider layouts may place the inspection frame beside them, never ahead of them.

rules.name: The Tonal-First Rule
rules.body: Establish hierarchy with surface contrast and borders before reaching for shadow.

rules.name: The No Glow Rule
rules.body: Do not use neon bloom, frosted glass, or glow-heavy cyber effects; the inspection language comes from measured geometry and honest state.

rules.name: The Restrained Curve Rule
rules.body: Default to the smallest radius and increase it only when the component already establishes that role; never turn the system into pill-shaped generic commerce UI.

dos: Do lead mobile surfaces with search, selection, or another usable shopping action.
Do use graphite, paper, borders, rails, ticks, and compact labels to create the technical atmosphere.
Do preserve Arabic RTL and English LTR equivalence with logical layout properties.
Do keep routine motion between 160ms and 240ms, using the calibrated easing curve for spatial movement.
Do use honest labels and configured routes when vehicle data or commercial proof is unavailable.
donts: Don't turn the hero into a cinematic car poster that delays product discovery.
Don't use glow-heavy cyber effects, frosted glass, or generic glass panels.
Don't spread orange across large backgrounds or introduce competing accent colors.
Don't default to pill controls, oversized rounding, or generic ecommerce cards.
Don't claim real vehicle-to-part fitment, statistics, testimonials, or proof that the product does not supply.
